Requester authorizes independent randomized complex photographic concepts and reference-image generation for actual color-keyword fidelity testing. Coordinator lane labels are experimental choices, not requester definitions. Independently interpret Split Complementary as a dominant hue with two neighbors of its opposite, Color Echo as separated repeated chromatic accents, and Color Framing as colored peripheral structures visibly enclosing the subject.

Create a photographic editorial of a mountain weather observer measuring a brass rain gauge at a remote observatory after a passing storm. Use the attached portrait as the appearance reference for her facial structure, dark eyes, and long wavy dark hair. She stands on the broad dry stone threshold, both boots planted apart; her left hand steadies the upright graduated cylinder on a waist-high stone ledge while her right hand holds its detached brass funnel beside it. The cylinder base rests flat on the ledge and a clear water meniscus catches the light. Her face and both hands remain visible in a three-quarter view. Beyond her, mist separates pine-covered slopes and a small observatory roof. A dominant deep blue field formed by the observatory doorway and storm clouds is balanced by separate yellow-orange and red-orange accents in a split complementary color relationship. A yellow-orange woven scarf is echoed by a small yellow-orange enamel gauge marker and a distant yellow-orange roof panel, linking foreground, subject, and background through color echo. Deep blue painted doorway uprights occupy the left and right image margins, forming color framing around the observer and her warm scarf. Let the brass show damp engraved texture, the hair remain softly wind-tossed, and the face retain natural skin detail. Compose a coherent environmental portrait with legible weather-measuring action and layered mountain depth.
